A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Perinucleus fingerprinting work. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and complete appendices are readable and support matching content despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original fingerprinting experiments, utility and persistence measurements, robustness tests, and collusion simulations in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds results on DPO, additional attacks and models, computational costs, and comparisons with MergePrint.

M1.justification: Perinucleus sampling, regularized training, collusion assignment and detection, and Algorithms 1–2 remain unchanged. Model-Averaging is renamed Weight Deviation Penalty with the same update. Multiple-response fingerprints, prompt training, meta-learning, and parameter expansion already appear in v1.

E1.justification: v2 adds Orca preference pairs for DPO and WildChat prompts as a natural-query reference. GRI reflection attacks and merging two fingerprinted models add test scenarios within the existing robustness task. OpenLLM, Alpaca, and MathInstruct coverage remains.

E2.justification: MergePrint is only discussed in v1, whereas v2 evaluates a reimplementation and its OptI component in Appendix F.7 and Table 6. v2 also adds ENGLISH-RANDOM comparisons for retained Mistral and Llama-Instruct evaluations that previously showed only Perinucleus results. This materially expands comparator coverage.

E3.justification: The model configuration matrix expands to ten models, adding OLMo-2, Qwen-2.5, and Phi-3 configurations while removing Gemma. New protocols include an SFT epoch sweep, one epoch of DPO after Alpaca SFT, and shared-versus-disjoint fingerprint merging. The 50,000-sample MathInstruct control in v1 Figure 12 is removed.

E4.justification: v2 adds epoch sensitivity, DPO robustness, collusive merging, GRI attacks, qualitative completion failures, and analysis separating MergePrint components. Conversely, v1 Figure 4's persistence comparison across model sizes disappears. The regularization ablation and response-transfer analyses are retained through relocation or redrawing, rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Both versions report three runs and mean/standard deviation for the main results. v2 newly identifies Figure 5 as single-seed and clarifies optimization and fingerprint-generation randomness in Appendix D. These are reporting refinements; an increase or reduction in repeated runs is not established.

E6.justification: v2 adds numerous results, including 97% accuracy under GRI and over 95% persistence of shared fingerprints after collusive merging. Table 6 reports MergePrint versus Perinucleus scores of 70.0 versus 69.8 at 1,024 fingerprints. SFT sensitivity values change, while Gemma and small-model persistence results disappear. These are additions, revisions, and removals, not demonstrated same-setting performance improvements.

T1.justification: The false-positive bound, collusion bound, unanimous-response assumption, and Appendix B proofs are retained. v2's explicit parameter quantifiers and queried-fingerprint wording clarify mathematics already present in v1's proofs; they do not introduce a new theoretical result or derivation.

C1.justification: The central claims remain scalable, harmless, persistent fingerprinting, insertion of 24,576 fingerprints into Llama-3.1-8B, and security benefits from scalability. Expanded model results support the existing generalization claim rather than redefine the main contribution.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly discusses the limitation posed by attackers using unrelated models and leaves stronger adaptive sampling attacks unresolved. It also links unusual completions to low-probability response tokens, attributes GRI robustness to semantic alignment, and explains MergePrint insertion instability through its objective. These add bounded interpretations and qualifications.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-repository link, detailed explanations of baseline adaptations, and disclosure of the MergePrint reimplementation. Appendix D.5 and Table 2 newly report four L40 GPUs, convergence epochs, and wall-clock times. These substantially expand reproducibility and resource information beyond v1's existing training and generation settings.

R1.justification: Most of the related-work survey is retained. v2 adds IMF and context-free synthetic-data work, sources for new models and post-training experiments, and critical positioning against the previously cited MergePrint. Gemma and Training AI to be Loyal references are removed.

P1.justification: The narrative is substantially reorganized: related work is compressed, response-design and ablation material moves into Appendix F, and post-training analysis moves into Section 4.2. Security explanations and captions are extensively revised, Appendix F is reordered, and a Broader Impact section is added.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to one. v1's ablation table becomes v2 Figure 12; model and post-training figures are expanded and rearranged. New completion, timing, and MergePrint tables appear, and histogram axes and legends change. Numerous retained displays are relocated.

improvement.justification: Additional robustness tests, model and baseline comparisons, and code/resource disclosures strengthen validation and reproducibility information. The net gain is limited by removal of the matched-size MathInstruct control and small-model persistence analysis. New Table 2 also reports convergence runs up to 90 epochs without reconciling them with Appendix D's retained 40-epoch limit. The core method, theory, and headline findings remain stable.
